generatedProse.concept-context: Across the School of Sport, referencing is how you credit the studies, data and ideas your work builds on. The school spans several subjects, from sport and exercise science to coaching, sport management and sport therapy, and they share a focus on performance, physical activity and health. They differ in their evidence: a physiology lab reports test data, a coach draws on training observation, a management team weighs participation figures. Whatever the subject, a reference records whose work a claim came from and where it was published. That lets a reader separate your own thinking from the research behind it, and it credits the people who produced that research.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two sport and exercise science students using the same physiology journal article in an essay.

Tom uses the study's finding on recovery and, at the end, adds the article to a reference list so he is not accused of copying. The source is listed, but Tom treats referencing only as a way of staying out of trouble, added once the writing is done. Whether the finding is clearly credited where he uses it, or whether the list shows his reading, has not really been considered. This treats referencing as a chore.

Amara references the same article as she uses the finding, naming the authors in the text and giving the full details in the list. For Amara, the reference credits the researchers whose data this is, keeps her own thinking separate from theirs, and shows the tutor the literature behind her argument. Avoiding plagiarism follows from this, rather than being the whole point.

Both students listed the source. Only Amara used referencing for what it is really for: crediting research and evidencing her reading.
generatedProse.summary: Across the School of Sport, referencing is how you acknowledge the studies and data your work builds on, not a chore bolted on at the end. You can now explain what referencing is and why it matters: it credits the researchers whose findings you use, it is part of academic integrity, and it shows a tutor the evidence behind your work. The next lessons turn this purpose into practice: the styles and parts of a reference, and how to reference accurately when you quote and paraphrase.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's use of the reference go beyond avoiding plagiarism?

items.text: Crediting the researchers' finding and showing the evidence behind her argument.
Listing the article once the essay was finished.
Using more studies than Tom did.
Leaving out quotation marks so her writing looked original.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara referenced to credit the researchers and evidence her reading, not just to avoid plagiarism.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what the reference did beyond keeping Amara out of trouble.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara used the reference to credit the researchers' finding and show the evidence behind her work. Listing late, piling up studies or hiding a borrowing are not the point.
